:::{#thm-entropy-quantization}
#### Entropy of a quantized random variable

Let $X$ be a [continuous random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-continuous-rv)
whose [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf) is [continuous](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-integration.html#def-continuous),
and whose [entropy](#def-entropy) is a [Riemann integral](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-integration.html#def-riemann-integral) whose value is not $\pm\infty$
(an improper one if the support of the density is unbounded).
For a bin width $\Delta > 0$,
let $X^\Delta$ be the [discrete random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-discrete-rv) that records the bin of $X$:
$X^\Delta = x_i$ when $i\Delta \le X < (i+1)\Delta$,
for $i \in \bbZ$, so that every $\Delta$ has infinitely many bins,
where $x_i$ is a point of that bin
with $\p(X=x_i)\,\Delta = \P(i\Delta \le X < (i+1)\Delta)$.
Then

$$\entropyf{X^\Delta} + \log \Delta \to \entropyf{X} \quad \text{as } \Delta \to 0.$$

[@cover2006elements, Theorem 8.3.1]

:::

::: proof

Because the [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf) is [continuous](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-integration.html#def-continuous),
in every bin it takes the value $\P(i\Delta \le X < (i+1)\Delta)/\Delta$ at some point of that bin.
If the density is [constant](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-constant-function) on the bin,
any point of the bin takes that value.
Otherwise the value lies strictly between the [minimum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-basics.html#def-minimum) and the [maximum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-basics.html#def-maximum) of the density on the closed bin,
so by [continuity](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-integration.html#def-continuous) the density takes it at a point strictly between the two,
which is inside the bin.
That point is the $x_i$ of the stated choice.
By the choice of $x_i$,
the [probability mass](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf) of $X^\Delta$ at $x_i$ is $\P(X^\Delta = x_i) = \p(X=x_i)\,\Delta$.
By @thm-entropy-discrete,
with each [sum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-summation) over the bins of positive [probability](probability-basics.qmd#def-probability)
(a bin of probability $0$ adds nothing to the [entropy](#def-entropy)),

$$
\ba
\entropyf{X^\Delta}
&= -\sum_i \p(X=x_i)\,\Delta \log \paren{\p(X=x_i)\,\Delta} \\
&= -\sum_i \Delta\, \p(X=x_i) \log \p(X=x_i) - \sum_i \p(X=x_i)\,\Delta \log \Delta && \text{(log of a product)} \\
&= -\sum_i \Delta\, \p(X=x_i) \log \p(X=x_i) - \log \Delta. && \text{(the masses sum to } 1 \text{)}
\ea
$$

Adding $\log \Delta$ to both sides leaves the first [sum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-summation),
which is a [Riemann sum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-integration.html#def-riemann-sum) for $-\int \p(X=x) \log \p(X=x)\, dx$.
By @thm-entropy-continuous, its value is $\entropyf{X}$,
and a Riemann sum [converges](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-integration.html#thm-riemann-general) to its [Riemann integral](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-integration.html#def-riemann-integral) as $\Delta \to 0$.
When the support is unbounded,
the hypothesis includes that these [Riemann sums](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-integration.html#def-riemann-sum) converge to the entropy.

:::
